**Test Image Analysis:**
- **Plant part:** Leaf (tomato leaf with serrated edges)
- **Key features:** Yellow patches with brown necrotic centers, multiple affected leaves, yellowing with brown/tan spots

**Leaf candidates narrowed (13 classes from part_index):**
Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato, Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus, Early_Blight, Gray_Mold, Late_Blight, Leaf_Mold, Powdery_Mildew, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Verticillium_Wilt

Now viewing reference images. Starting with one from each major candidate:

**Summary of Reference Image Comparisons:**

| Class | Visual Match |
|-------|---|
| Early_Blight | Dark brown lesions, less yellow overall |
| Late_Blight | Gray-brown patches, water-soaked appearance |
| Leaf_Mold | Overall dark discoloration on lower surface |
| Powdery_Mildew | White/light lesions on green leaves |
| **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch** | **Yellow background with small dark brown spots - STRONG MATCH** |
| Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus | Large necrotic/bronzed areas |
| Verticillium_Wilt | One-sided yellowing, V-shaped pattern |
| Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus | Mosaic mottling with leaf distortion |

**Visual Analysis:**

The test image shows a distinctive pattern of **yellow/lime background with scattered small dark brown lesions**, which most closely matches the Septoria_Leaf_Blotch reference image (CDDM_1006.jpg). The lesions appear circular, small, and evenly distributed across multiple leaves with a characteristic yellowish halo effect around brown spots.

This pattern distinctly differs from:
- Early_Blight (larger, darker, concentric rings)
- Late_Blight (gray-brown, water-soaked)
- Verticillium_Wilt (asymmetric yellowing with V-shape)
- Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus (large necrotic areas)

{"prediction": "Septoria_Leaf_Blotch", "confidence": 0.82, "reasoning": "Yellow leaf background with small dark brown circular lesions matches Septoria_Leaf_Blotch reference image. Pattern shows multiple small spots scattered across leaves, consistent with pycnidia-bearing lesions <1/8 inch. Differs from early blight (which shows concentric rings) and late blight (gray-brown water-soaked appearance)."}
